contentText: A surprising new study suggests that when and how often older adults nap could reveal hidden warning signs about their health. Researchers followed 1,338 people for up to 19 years and discovered that longer, more frequent naps were linked to higher mortality, while morning nappers faced a 30% greater risk of death than afternoon nappers. Each additional hour of daytime sleep was associated with a 13% increase in mortality risk.
